title: Anatomy: 206 Bones
description: For anatomy learners: the conventional 206 adult bones, counted individually by side and digit, with location and a notable feature. Counts vary with fusion and accessory bones; verify with current guidelines for clinical use.

cards.back: Location: anterior skull. Region: axial skeleton; skull. Notable feature: forms the forehead and roof of the orbits.
Location: posterior and inferior skull. Region: axial skeleton; skull. Notable feature: contains the foramen magnum.
Location: central skull base. Region: axial skeleton; skull. Notable feature: contains the sella turcica that houses the pituitary gland.
Location: between the orbits at the anterior skull base. Region: axial skeleton; skull. Notable feature: its cribriform plate transmits olfactory nerve fibers.
Location: lower jaw. Region: axial skeleton; skull. Notable feature: the only freely movable bone of the skull apart from the auditory ossicles.
Location: midline nasal cavity. Region: axial skeleton; skull. Notable feature: forms the inferior-posterior part of the bony nasal septum.
Location: left superior-lateral cranium. Region: axial skeleton; skull. Notable feature: joins its opposite partner at the sagittal suture.
Location: left lateral skull base. Region: axial skeleton; skull. Notable feature: contains structures of the middle and inner ear.
Location: left upper jaw. Region: axial skeleton; skull. Notable feature: bears upper teeth and contributes to the hard palate.
Location: left cheek and lateral orbit. Region: axial skeleton; skull. Notable feature: forms part of the zygomatic arch.

Location: left medial wall of the orbit. Region: axial skeleton; skull. Notable feature: contributes to the groove for the lacrimal drainage apparatus.

Location: left lateral wall of the nasal cavity. Region: axial skeleton; skull. Notable feature: a separate curved bone that increases nasal mucosal surface area.

Location: left middle ear. Region: axial skeleton; auditory ossicles. Notable feature: connects the malleus to the stapes.
Location: left middle ear. Region: axial skeleton; auditory ossicles. Notable feature: its footplate occupies the oval window; it is the smallest named human bone.
